questions.question: In a static leakage test, what is the maximum air loss allowed per minute for a triple combination vehicle with air brakes?
questions.explanation: In a static leakage test, a triple combination vehicle with air brakes should lose no more than 5 psi per minute. If air leaks faster, the vehicle needs repair and should not be driven.

questions.question: What is the average reaction time for a driver?

options.text: Between three-quarters of a second and one second

questions.correctAnswerText: Between three-quarters of a second and one second
questions.explanation: The average driver's reaction time is between three-quarters of a second and one second.

questions.question: Where should your vehicle's final position be?

options.text: Exactly where the examiner told you to park it.
Within five feet of where the examiner said.
Within two feet of where the examiner said.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exactly where the examiner told you to park it.
questions.explanation: You must park your vehicle in the exact position the examiner describes. Not parking exactly as instructed can result in losing points or failing the basic control skills test.

questions.question: A 40-foot item on a flatbed trailer must be secured with at least how many tie-downs?
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo length. All cargo needs at least two tie-downs, no matter the size.

questions.question: When operating a CMV, what is required regarding safety belts?

options.text: You do not have to wear one.
You only need to wear one if the vehicle has no airbags.
You only need to wear one if carrying more than 1,000 pounds of cargo.

questions.explanation: A safety belt is your best protection in a crash. You must always wear a safety belt when operating a CMV.

questions.question: Which vehicles must have emergency brakes?
questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes. These brakes must use mechanical force to hold.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a header board?

options.text: They protect the driver from cargo shifting forward.
They protect the driver's head when entering the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: They protect the driver from cargo shifting forward.
questions.explanation: Header boards, also called "headache racks," protect the driver if cargo moves forward during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: If your truck or trailer catches fire, where should you park it?

options.text: In a busy area near trees.
In an open area away from other things.

questions.correctAnswerText: In an open area away from other things.
questions.explanation: If there is a fire, leave the road and stop in an open area away from things that could catch fire, like plants or other vehicles. Do not stop at a service station.

questions.question: If your ABS stops working while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Use the parking brake to stop.

questions.explanation: If the ABS is not working, the basic brakes still work. Continue driving and braking as you normally would.

questions.question: At what air pressure level does an air compressor governor stop pumping air into the tanks?
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops pumping when the air tanks reach 125 psi. This is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: When entering traffic, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Wait for a large gap between vehicles.
Be ready for your vehicle to accelerate slowly, especially if it is loaded.
Make sure you can cross all the way across traffic without getting in the way.
Assume other drivers will make room for your larger vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers will make room for your larger vehicle.
questions.explanation: When crossing or entering traffic, think about how big your vehicle is and how much space it needs to speed up. Wait for a gap in traffic that is large enough for your vehicle. You will need more room to accelerate if your vehicle is carrying a heavy load. Before crossing, make sure you can get all the way across without blocking traffic.

questions.question: If you must drive in reverse, it is helpful to:

options.text: Drive as fast as possible to finish quickly.
Exit the truck and walk the path to check for obstacles.
Use only the passenger side mirror.
Stick your head out the window and look backward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the truck and walk the path to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before driving in reverse, walk around the vehicle to check for hazards in your path. Use the mirrors on both sides while backing. Always back up slowly.

questions.question: Looking far ahead while driving is:

options.text: Discouraged because there is little you can do about hazards far away.
Only encouraged when carrying hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to spot hazards early and react properly.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:

options.text: Push the brake pedal down quickly.
Press the brake pedal repeatedly, but do not hold it down continuously.
Use the same amount of brake pressure every time you stop.

questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal smoothly and gradually each time you slow down or stop. The amount of brake pressure needed depends on your speed and how fast you need to stop.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Complete the test without an accident.
Show that you can use your cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that you can use your cell phone while driving.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, you must drive safely and responsibly. Wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs and laws, and complete the test with no accidents or violations.

questions.question: How often should you drain air tanks with manual drains?
questions.explanation: Drain manual air tank drains at the end of each driving day. This prevents oil and water from building up in the tanks.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal, air pressure activates a switch and:

options.text: Turns on the low pressure warning light.
Turns off the low pressure warning light.

questions.explanation: In a vehicle with air brakes, pressing the brake pedal activates an electric switch that turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: When carrying a wide load, you should:

options.text: Get special permits and follow special rules.
Honk at other drivers to move out of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get special permits and follow special rules.
questions.explanation: Wide, long, or heavy loads require special permits. These vehicles can usually only be driven at certain times.

questions.question: When using mirrors while driving, you should:

options.text: Look in the mirrors for short periods.
Look in the mirrors for long periods.
Use only the driver's side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look in the mirrors for short periods.
questions.explanation: Staring at mirrors for too long is dangerous. You will travel a long distance without looking at the road ahead.

questions.question: A person working on a broken-down vehicle on the road shoulder:

options.text: Will likely watch traffic on the road.
May be focused on repairs and not notice traffic.
Does not have to follow traffic laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be focused on repairs and not notice traffic.
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people fixing broken-down vehicles. They may be focused on the repair and not see traffic or other hazards.

questions.question: When driving through a work zone, what should you do?

options.text: Steer with one hand to keep the other hand free.

questions.explanation: In work zones, follow the posted speed limits. Slow down if the road or weather is bad. Slow down even more if workers are near the road.

questions.question: If your engine catches fire, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Turn the engine off as soon as possible.
Spray foam from under the vehicle.

questions.explanation: If your engine catches fire, turn off the engine right away. Do not open the hood if you can help it. Spray foam through the louvers or from under the vehicle instead.

questions.question: Which statement about turn signals is correct?

options.text: A driver does not need to tell others about their plans.
A driver should only use turn signals if another vehicle is beside them.
A driver should not use a turn signal if the lane change is obvious.
A driver should always use turn signals to tell others about their plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver should always use turn signals to tell others about their plans.
questions.explanation: Always use turn signals. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: When checking engine belts during a vehicle inspection test, what is true?

options.text: Belts should be tight, with up to three inches of play.
You do not need to check the water pump belt.
You should remove the air compressor belt.
You must identify which parts are not belt-driven, if any.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must identify which parts are not belt-driven, if any.
questions.explanation: Check the power steering, water pump, alternator, and air compressor belts for cracks and frays. Allow up to three-quarters of an inch of play in the center of each belt. If any of these parts are not belt-driven, you must identify them. Make sure they work properly, are not damaged or leaking, and are mounted securely.

questions.question: If your vehicle is hydroplaning, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, do not use the brakes. Instead, release the gas pedal and push in the clutch. This will slow your vehicle and help it get traction back.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, what will you be asked to do?

options.text: Explain what you would check and why.
Estimate the weight of a trailer load.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you would check and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must inspect your vehicle and explain to the examiner what you are checking and why.

questions.question: Why are roads most slippery right after rain starts?

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Gravel gets washed to the middle of the lane.
Some tires are not made for rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, it mixes with oil that has dripped onto the road. This creates a slippery and dangerous surface.

questions.question: If asked to back your vehicle into an alley, what should you do first?

options.text: Pull directly into the alley parking space.
Turn your vehicle right to face the alley.
Pull past the alley and stop at a right angle to the edge.
Pull past the alley and stop parallel to the edge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull past the alley and stop parallel to the edge.
questions.explanation: Pull past the alley and stop parallel to the edge. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley parking space. Your vehicle should be parked straight within the parking boundaries.

questions.question: The front of an enclosed trailer should:
questions.explanation: When inspecting an enclosed trailer, check the front for damage such as cracks, bulges, or holes.

questions.question: A 40-foot load must be secured with a minimum of how many tie-downs?
questions.explanation: Cargo on flatbed trailers must be tied down. Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. Use at least two tie-downs, regardless of cargo size.

questions.question: How often should you test the low pressure warning signal?
questions.explanation: Your low pressure warning light must work properly. After the system charges, test it by quickly pressing and releasing the brake pedal. This releases air from the brake system. The warning signal should turn on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: Heavy steering usually means:
questions.explanation: Heavy steering usually means a front tire has failed. If your steering feels different, safely pull off the road as soon as possible and check your tires.

questions.question: Bridges usually:

options.text: Freeze only when the temperature drops well below 32 degrees Fahrenheit.

questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before regular road surfaces. Drive extra carefully when crossing bridges if the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: What can change how tall a vehicle sits?
questions.explanation: A heavy load makes a vehicle sit lower than normal. An empty vehicle will be taller than one carrying a heavy load. If your vehicle fits under an overpass when full, it may not fit when empty.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:
questions.explanation: If tailgated, increase the space between you and the car ahead. This helps you avoid sudden stops that could cause a rear-end crash and makes it easier for the tailgater to pass. Speeding up only creates more danger by encouraging faster tailgating.

questions.question: Overloading cargo can harm all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Overloading a vehicle damages steering, braking, and speed control. Pay attention to how your vehicle handles when you add weight.

questions.question: If your tractor has ABS but your trailer does not, the ABS:

options.text: Will still help your steering control.
Will help others see when you brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will still help your steering control.
questions.explanation: When only the tractor has ABS, it still improves steering control. Watch your trailer and reduce braking pressure if it starts to swing out.

questions.question: When driving, hold the steering wheel:

options.text: With both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.
With both hands at the bottom of the wheel.
With both hands at the top of the wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: With both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands. Place them on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: If you see a distracted driver, you should:
questions.explanation: Give a distracted driver plenty of space. Be careful when passing because the driver may not see you and drift into your lane.

questions.question: When driving, you should:

options.text: Only use turn signals when other vehicles are near.
Not use turn signals in construction zones.
Always use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Communicate your plans to other drivers. Always signal before turning or changing lanes, even if no other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: During the basic vehicle control skills test, what is a pull-up?

options.text: A pull-up always counts against you.
You must do at least one pull-up.
Just stopping without changing direction is not a pull-up.
Some test administrators think too many pull-ups are okay.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just stopping without changing direction is not a pull-up.
questions.explanation: A pull-up happens when you stop and move forward to get a better position. Stopping without changing direction is not a pull-up. Doing too many pull-ups will count as errors.

questions.question: Which crime would NOT disqualify someone from getting a hazardous materials endorsement?
questions.explanation: Several crimes disqualify a person from getting a hazardous materials endorsement for seven years. These include kidnapping, smuggling, and immigration violations. More serious crimes like murder result in a lifetime ban.

questions.question: What do move over laws require?

options.text: Trucks must use the left lane.
All vehicles must move out of the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights.
All vehicles must use the left lane.
All vehicles must move to the left lane when a flatbed trailer is in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles must move out of the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights on is stopped on the side of the road, you must leave the lane next to it if you safely can. If you cannot move over safely, slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: What does poor weight balance do to a vehicle?

options.text: It improves how the vehicle handles.
It makes the vehicle harder to handle.
It makes the vehicle easier to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It makes the vehicle harder to handle.
questions.explanation: When a load is not balanced properly, it makes the vehicle harder and more unsafe to handle.

questions.question: What tool should you use to check if tires are properly inflated?
questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check tire pressure during the vehicle inspection test. Just kicking the tires will not pass the inspection.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: They allow rainwater to enter the tanks.
They remove water and oil from the tanks.
They must stay open while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: They remove water and oil from the tanks.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. If this water and oil build up, they can damage your brakes.

questions.question: How must cargo be secured on a flatbed trailer or open trailer?

options.text: It can be loose so it shifts when the vehicle turns.
It just needs to be heavy enough not to shift.

questions.explanation: Cargo on flatbed or open trailers must be securely tied down. This keeps it from shifting or falling off while the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of drowsiness while driving?
questions.explanation: Drowsy driving is dangerous. Warning signs include lots of blinking, eyes closing or losing focus, frequent yawning, and drifting between lanes.

questions.question: When you start the vehicle during pre-trip inspection, what should the coolant temperature do?
questions.explanation: After starting your vehicle, watch the temperature gauge. The coolant temperature should gradually increase to its normal operating range.

questions.question: What can a modulating control valve control?
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets you gradually apply spring brakes. On equipped vehicles, a lever on the dashboard controls this valve.
